name: Syabrubesi
blurb: The roadhead where the Langtang Khola meets the Bhote Koshi, and the classic start for Langtang and the Tamang Heritage Trail. The Bhote Koshi flood of 26 August 2026 badly damaged the town and cut its road; check access before you plan around it.
tip: After the flood, Langtang groups were starting from Dhunche and Thulo Syabru instead. Ask your agency which lodges and bridges here are back in use.

name: Dhunche
blurb: The district headquarters of Rasuwa, strung along the highway high above the Trishuli gorge. Langtang National Park permits are checked at the entrance to town, and the steep trail to Gosaikunda starts just beyond it.
tip: With the road to Syabrubesi cut by the August 2026 flood, Dhunche has also been the working roadhead for the Langtang valley.

name: Thulo Bharkhu
blurb: A village on the highway between Dhunche and Syabrubesi, where the old foot trail to Thulo Syabru leaves the road and climbs through forest to Brabal. Little used for years, it is an approach to Langtang again since the 2026 flood.

name: Thulo Syabru
blurb: A Tamang village strung down a steep spur between the Langtang Khola and the Gosaikunda ridge, and the link between the two treks. With the Syabrubesi road cut by the August 2026 flood, Langtang valley treks have been starting from here.
tip: Lodges at the top of the village have the views and the shorter start for Chandanbari; those lower down suit an early descent to the Langtang Khola.

name: Bamboo
blurb: A handful of lodges in a damp, shaded bend of the Langtang Khola gorge, named for the bamboo thickets around them. It is the usual lunch stop on the first day; the trail from Thulo Syabru joins the valley route a short way downstream.

name: Rimche
blurb: A few lodges on a more open perch about twenty minutes below Lama Hotel, where the high trail from Sherpagaon comes in. It is sunnier than its neighbour, and usually the place with beds when Lama Hotel is full.

name: Lama Hotel
blurb: Not one hotel but a cluster of lodges in thick forest beside the Langtang Khola, and the standard first night of the trek. The gorge is narrow here, so it gets little sun and no mountain view.
tip: Rooms run short in October and November. Arrive by mid-afternoon or have your guide phone ahead.

name: Ghodatabela
blurb: A few lodges and an army and national park checkpost at the point where the forest ends and the valley opens into a broad glacial trough. The name means horse stable. The first clear views of Langtang Lirung come around here.

name: Thangshyap
blurb: A line of lodges in yak pasture between Ghodatabela and Langtang village. Stopping here rather than pushing on to Langtang village trims the day's height gain when the altitude is starting to tell.

name: Langtang Village
blurb: The valley's main village. The old settlement was buried by an avalanche and landslide set off by the earthquake of 25 April 2015, which killed more than 240 people here; the rebuilt village and its lodges stand just up-valley of the debris.
tip: A memorial to those who died stands at the old site. Walk through quietly; most families here lost relatives.

name: Mundu
blurb: A small stone village half an hour beyond Langtang village, with a few quieter lodges among walled fields. Long mani walls line the trail on either side of it.

name: Kyanjin Gompa
blurb: The last settlement in the Langtang valley: a wide cluster of lodges around a small monastery and a yak-cheese factory, ringed by Langtang Lirung, Kimshung and Naya Kanga. Every side trip in the upper valley starts here.
tip: Stay two nights. The day hikes are the point of the trek, and the second night makes them far more comfortable.

name: Kyanjin Ri
blurb: The ridge directly behind Kyanjin Gompa. Prayer flags on a lower shoulder at about 4,300 m are often taken for the top; the true summit at 4,773 m is another hour up a steep, exposed crest and looks straight onto the Lirung glacier.
tip: The lower shoulder is a worthwhile goal in itself if the wind is up or you are feeling the height.

name: Tserko Ri
blurb: A 4,984 m walk-up summit east of Kyanjin Gompa, often advertised as 5,033 m. The climb needs no scrambling, but it gains more than 1,100 m and takes most of a day; the top gives a full circle of peaks from Langtang Lirung round to Gangchempo and Dorje Lakpa.
tip: Leave by 6 am. Cloud usually builds on the summit by late morning and the way down is long.

name: Langshisha Kharka
blurb: A yak pasture at the head of the open valley, a long and almost level day walk east of Kyanjin Gompa. There are no lodges on the way, so carry food and water for eight or nine hours and turn back by midday.

name: Ganja La
blurb: A glaciated pass of about 5,120 m south of Kyanjin Gompa that links the Langtang valley with Helambu. It needs a camping crew, rope and ice axe and a guide who knows the route, and snow closes it for much of the year.

name: Sherpagaon
blurb: A small village high on the sunny north side of the Langtang Khola gorge, on the upper trail between Syabrubesi and Rimche. Its lodges are an alternative first or last night for trekkers who would rather stay out of the valley floor.

name: Chandanbari
blurb: A lodge village on the forested ridge above Dhunche, also called Sing Gompa after its small monastery. A yak-cheese factory operates here, and it is the usual first night on the way up to Gosaikunda.
tip: You are already 1,370 m above Dhunche. If you have a headache here, spend a second night rather than going higher.

name: Cholangpati
blurb: A few lodges at the tree line on the ridge between Chandanbari and Laurebina, quoted at 3,584 m or about 3,650 m, where the forest gives way to open hillside. A sensible place to break the climb to Gosaikunda if Laurebina feels too high for the night.

name: Laurebina
blurb: A row of lodges on an open ridge at 3,910 m with one of the widest views on the trek: the Annapurnas, Manaslu, Ganesh Himal and Langtang Lirung in a single sweep. Sleeping here splits the height gain between Chandanbari and the lake.

name: Gosaikunda
blurb: A dark alpine lake at 4,380 m, sacred to Shiva and the goal of a large pilgrimage at the Janai Purnima full moon in August. Lodges line the slope above its northern shore; Bhairav Kunda and Saraswati Kunda lie just below.
tip: This is the highest night of the trek and it comes quickly. Do not climb here from Chandanbari in one day if you had any symptoms there.

name: Laurebina La
blurb: The 4,610 m pass between Gosaikunda and Helambu, reached past a string of small lakes above the main one. The climb from the lodges is short, but the descent east to Phedi is long, rocky and without shelter, and snow can close it from December to March.

name: Phedi
blurb: A couple of basic lodges at the foot of the eastern side of the Laurebina La, the first shelter after the pass. Its height is quoted anywhere between 3,630 and 3,740 m. A useful stop if the crossing has taken longer than planned.

name: Ghopte
blurb: A few simple lodges beside rock overhangs on the rough traverse between Phedi and Tharepati. The trail on either side crosses ravine after ravine through rhododendron and juniper, and is slow going in rain, mist or snow.

name: Tharepati
blurb: A windy ridge-top group of lodges where the trail from Gosaikunda meets the Helambu circuit, quoted between 3,640 and 3,690 m. It is the highest night on the Helambu trek, with a dawn view east to Dorje Lakpa and the Jugal peaks.

name: Magin Goth
blurb: A few simple lodges in a forest clearing at about 3,285 m, between Kutumsang and Tharepati. Breaking the climb here keeps the day's height gain to roughly 800 m and makes the night at Tharepati easier.

name: Kutumsang
blurb: A lodge village in a saddle on the Helambu ridge, where the Langtang National Park checkpost inspects permits. Above here the trail leaves the farmland and climbs through forest, with no villages until Tharepati.

name: Golphu Bhanjyang
blurb: A Tamang village in a notch on the ridge between Chipling and Kutumsang, with several lodges and a few shops. Many groups stop here for lunch on the long day from Chisapani.

name: Chipling
blurb: A Tamang village on a steep slope above Pati Bhanjyang, reached by a long flight of stone steps. A handful of lodges make it a quieter overnight stop than Chisapani for groups that start early from Sundarijal.

name: Pati Bhanjyang
blurb: A farming village in a saddle about 400 m below Chisapani, with a few lodges and shops. From here the Helambu trail starts the climb up the ridge toward Chipling.

name: Melamchi Gaun
blurb: A Hyolmo village on a sunny terrace beneath Tharepati, with a gompa, apple orchards and a meditation cave linked to Guru Rinpoche. It faces Tarkeghyang across the deep valley of the Melamchi Khola.

name: Tarkeghyang
blurb: The largest Hyolmo village in Helambu, on a shelf below Ama Yangri with a monastery at its centre. Most of its houses were destroyed by the 2015 earthquake and have been rebuilt; a rough jeep road now reaches it from Timbu.

name: Sermathang
blurb: A spread-out Hyolmo village on a ridge, with several monasteries and a clear view north to the Jugal peaks. A jeep road links it to Melamchi, so many groups now end the Helambu walk here.

name: Melamchi Pul Bazaar
blurb: A hot, low market town at the meeting of the Melamchi and Indrawati rivers, and the traditional end of the Helambu trek. Debris floods in June 2021 destroyed the riverside part of the bazaar. Buses run from here to Kathmandu.

name: Timbu
blurb: The village at the head of the Melamchi valley road, at about 1,600 m, where buses from Kathmandu stop. It is the usual start for the climb to Tarkeghyang and Ama Yangri, and the quick way out of upper Helambu.

name: Ama Yangri
blurb: A 3,771 m summit above Tarkeghyang, revered by the Hyolmo as the protecting mother of Helambu. A stupa and prayer flags mark the top, which looks north to the Langtang, Dorje Lakpa and Jugal peaks.
tip: Be on top soon after sunrise. Cloud climbs out of the valleys by mid-morning for most of the year.

name: Gatlang
blurb: A large Tamang village of closely packed stone and timber houses on a terraced hillside, the best-known stop on the Tamang Heritage Trail. Community lodges and homestays take guests, and the small sacred lake of Parvati Kunda lies a short climb above.

name: Rongga Bhanjyang
blurb: A saddle at about 2,190 m on the ridge west of Syabrubesi, two hours' steep climb above the town. The first walking day of the Tamang Heritage Trail crosses it, with a view of Ganesh Himal and down over the terraces of Goljung.

name: Goljung
blurb: A Tamang farming village on the terraces between the Rongga Bhanjyang saddle and Gatlang, passed on the first walking day of the Tamang Heritage Trail. A dirt road links it to Syabrubesi and Chilime.

name: Chilime
blurb: A village on the Chilime Khola beside the headworks of the Chilime hydropower scheme, at the low point between Gatlang and Tatopani. The trail crosses the river on a suspension bridge near neighbouring Thambuchet before the long climb north.

name: Tatopani
blurb: A lodge village named for its hot springs, long the main draw of the Tamang Heritage Trail. The springs stopped flowing after the 2015 earthquake and reports of their return are unconfirmed, so ask in Gatlang before counting on a soak.

name: Brimdang
blurb: A small Tamang hamlet with a little gompa in the forest between Tatopani and the Nagthali ridge. Most trekkers only pass through on the climb, with a pause for tea.

name: Nagthali
blurb: A ridge-top meadow at 3,165 m and the high point of the Tamang Heritage Trail, with a small gompa and a few lodges. The view takes in Langtang Lirung, the Kerung peaks across the Tibetan border, Ganesh Himal and the Sanjen range.

name: Thuman
blurb: A Tamang village on a shelf high above the Bhote Koshi, with an old monastery and a tradition of song and dance evenings when groups stay. It is on the official list of the Rasuwa border restricted area, though checks have been rare.

name: Lingling
blurb: A small village on the Bhote Koshi valley road between Syabrubesi and Timure, at the foot of the climb to Briddim. This stretch of river was in the path of the August 2026 flood; ask locally which crossings and road sections are usable.

name: Briddim
blurb: A village of Tibetan descent on a hillside above the Bhote Koshi, run as a community homestay: guests are shared out among the families in turn, sleep in the household and eat with their hosts.

name: Timure
blurb: A roadside village on the Bhote Koshi a few kilometres short of the Rasuwagadhi border fort, once an optional night on the Tamang Heritage Trail. Reports say the flood of 26 August 2026 destroyed most of it; treat it as closed until told otherwise.
tip: It lies inside the Rasuwa border restricted area, so a visit needs the restricted-area permit as well as current local advice.

name: Chautara
blurb: The district headquarters of Sindhupalchok, a bazaar strung along a ridge between the Indrawati and Balephi valleys. Its hotels, shops and banks make it the last place to stock up before the ridge walk to Panch Pokhari.

name: Sano Okhareni
blurb: A farming village at about 1,965 m on the ridge north of Chautara, beyond the bazaar of Syaule, and the first night of the classic Panch Pokhari trek. A dirt road reaches it, so some groups start walking here. Thulo Okhareni is an hour further up.

name: Kami Kharka
blurb: A forest clearing and herders' pasture on the ridge above Thulo Okhareni, the second camp on the way to Panch Pokhari. Its height is given as anything from 2,730 to 2,870 m, and reports differ on whether a hut there offers beds.

name: Pauwa Bas
blurb: A campsite on the forested ridge at about 3,000 m, named after a pauwa, a rest house for pilgrims on their way to the lakes. One itinerary puts it at 3,250 m. Expect to camp, and have your guide show you where the water is.

name: Hille Bhanjyang
blurb: A camp in a notch of the ridge at about 3,400 m, between Pauwa Bas and Nasim Pati, where the forest thins to rhododendron and pasture. Groups pitch tents here; some agency pages mention a simple shelter, which we could not confirm.

name: Nasim Pati
blurb: Pilgrim shelters and a few seasonal teahouses on the ridge at about 3,700 m, where the trail from Bhotang meets the one from Chautara. It is the last night before the lakes, three to four hours above.
tip: The teahouses shut when their owners go down for the winter or after heavy snow. Have your guide phone ahead outside April, May, October and November.

name: Panch Pokhari
blurb: Five small lakes in a grassy bowl at about 4,100 m in Langtang National Park, sacred to Shiva and the goal of a large pilgrimage at the Janai Purnima full moon in August. A small shrine and a pilgrims' shelter stand by the water.
tip: Climb the rim behind the lakes at sunrise for the Jugal peaks. Cloud usually covers them by mid-morning.

name: Tupi Danda
blurb: A group of simple lodges on a forested spur at about 2,320 m, above Chhimti on the pilgrims' trail from Bhotang to Panch Pokhari. It is the first night up on the short route and the last on the long one, and has the highest phone signal on the trail.

name: Chhimti
blurb: The hamlet above Bhotang where the bus from Kathmandu ends and the pilgrims' trail to Panch Pokhari begins. A lodge or two take trekkers; outside the main seasons only one may be open.

name: Bhotang
blurb: A spread-out farming village high in the Indrawati valley, and the name most people use for the short route to Panch Pokhari. Buses from Kathmandu pass through on the way to the road end at Chhimti, and basic lodges and homestays take guests.

name: Dhap
blurb: A Tamang village on the terraces of the upper Indrawati valley, at about 1,250 m, and a night stop on the old walk out from Panch Pokhari to Melamchi Pul Bazaar. The valley road now passes it, so most trekkers go through by bus.

name: Parvati Kunda
blurb: A small sacred lake in a hollow of pasture and pine forest at about 2,600 m, an hour's climb above Gatlang. It is holy to Hindu and Buddhist pilgrims alike, and the trail to Somdang passes its shore.

name: Khurpu Bhanjyang
blurb: The forested pass between Gatlang and Somdang, at about 3,720 m; itineraries quote anything from 3,610 to 3,730 m. It is the first of the two passes on the Ruby Valley trek, and a climb of nearly 1,500 m from Gatlang.

name: Somdang
blurb: A few very simple lodges in a cold valley bottom at 3,271 m, on the border of Rasuwa and Dhading, near an abandoned lead and zinc mine. It is the usual night between Gatlang and the Pangsang La.
tip: Ask in Gatlang whether the lodges are open. In winter and in the monsoon they may be shut.

name: Pangsang La
blurb: A broad grassy saddle at about 3,842 m, the high point of the Ruby Valley trek, with Ganesh Himal to the north and Manaslu and the Langtang peaks on either hand. A simple lodge stands at the pass, and a rough road now reaches it from the Dhading side.

name: Tipling
blurb: A large Tamang and Ghale village on steep terraces below the Pangsang La, and the first homestay night in Ruby Valley. Its height is quoted between 1,890 and 2,078 m. A dirt road from Dhading Besi now reaches it.

name: Shertung
blurb: A large Tamang village on the hillside facing Tipling across the Adha Khola, a short climb above Chalish. Homestays take guests, and the village keeps its own dances and shaman traditions.

name: Chalish
blurb: A village of Gurung, Ghale and Kami families a short walk below Shertung, and the usual second homestay night in Ruby Valley. Hosts can point the way to a hot spring two to three hours off; ask whether the path is open.

name: Borang
blurb: A hillside village south-west of Chalish with a few homestays, at about 1,650 m; itineraries quote up to 1,700 m. Local jeeps for Dhading Besi start from the road below it, so for most groups the walking ends here.

name: Darkha
blurb: A hillside village in the Ankhu Khola valley, well south of Borang, and the last night on the longer walk out of Ruby Valley. Jeeps for Dhading Besi leave from Darkha Phedi in the valley below.

name: Dhading Besi
blurb: The district headquarters of Dhading, a low, warm bazaar town where the jeep road from Ruby Valley meets the buses for Kathmandu. Its link to the Prithvi Highway at Malekhu lost a bridge in the August 2026 flood; ask which road is in use.
